senses.en: A small flaw or sin.

examples.text: Voters were willing to forgive the candidate's youthful peccadilloes but not his dishonesty about them.

origin.ko: 스페인어 pecadillo, 즉 pecado(죄)에 지소사가 붙은 말로 '작은 죄'입니다.

senses.en: Out of the ordinary; odd; strange; unusual.

examples.text: The sky had a peculiar appearance before the storm.

senses.en: Common or usual for a certain place or circumstance; specific or particular.

examples.text: Kangaroos are peculiar to Australia.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pecūliāris '자기 소유의'에서 왔고, pecus는 '가축'입니다. 자기만의 것이라 남과 다르고 독특하다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: relating to or involving money

examples.text: He chose the degree for pecuniary reasons, but had no real interest in it.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pecūnia '돈'에서 왔고, 가축(pecū)이 곧 재산이었던 데서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: of or relating to pedagogy

examples.text: The school adopted a new pedagogical approach that emphasizes discussion over lectures.

origin.ko: pedagogy(교육학)에 -ical이 붙은 말로, 그리스어 '아이를 이끄는' 일에서 나왔습니다.

senses.en: A pedant; one who by teaching has become overly formal or pedantic in his or her ways; one who has the manner of a teacher.
senses.ko: 현학적인 교사, 훈장 티를 내는 사람

examples.text: The old pedagogue corrected every grammatical slip at the dinner table.

senses.en: someone who educates young people

examples.text: A gifted pedagogue, she made even difficult proofs seem approachable to beginners.

origin.ko: 그리스어 paidagōgós '아이를 이끄는 사람'에서 왔습니다. 아이를 이끌던 인도자가 지나치게 딱딱한 훈장 같은 교사를 뜻하게 되었습니다.

senses.en: marked by a narrow focus on or display of learning especially its trivial aspects

examples.text: His pedantic insistence on citing every source slowed the discussion to a crawl.

senses.en: sell or offer for sale from place to place

examples.text: Street vendors peddle cheap souvenirs to tourists near the cathedral.

senses.en: To spread or cause to spread.

examples.text: Christine walked a dangerous line, peddling gossip about her detested son-in-law.

origin.ko: pedlar(행상인)에서 거꾸로 만든 말로, burglar에서 burgle이 나온 것과 같은 방식입니다.

senses.en: lacking wit or imagination

examples.text: a pedestrian movie plot

senses.en: a person who travels by foot

examples.text: The new law requires drivers to yield to every pedestrian at the crosswalk.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pedester '걸어서 가는'에서 왔고, ped는 '발'입니다. 걸어 다니는 보통 수준이라 평범하고 재미없다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: Constantly complaining, especially in a childish way due to insignificant matters; fretful, whiny.

examples.text: Due to the long wait, there were several peevish patients in the doctor’s waiting room.

senses.en: Disparaging, belittling or derogatory.

examples.text: Critics used the term in a pejorative sense to dismiss the whole movement.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 peiōrāre '악화시키다'에서 왔고, peior는 '더 나쁜'입니다. 가치를 깎아내리는 말입니다.

senses.en: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable

examples.text: Written in spare, pellucid prose, the book reads like a close-to-the-bone memoir.

senses.en: transmitting light; able to be seen through with clarity

examples.text: Divers admired the pellucid water of the mountain lake.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pellūcidus '속까지 환히 비치는'에서 왔습니다. 빛이 통과할 만큼 투명하게 명쾌하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: a strong liking

examples.text: He has a penchant for fine wine.

origin.ko: 프랑스어 pencher '기울다'의 현재분사입니다. 마음이 한쪽으로 기우는 강한 취향입니다.

senses.en: Hanging from, or as if from, a support.

examples.text: Pendulous clusters of wisteria hung from the garden pergola.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pendulus '매달린'에서 왔고, pendeō는 '매달리다'입니다.

senses.en: feeling or expressing remorse for misdeeds

examples.text: The penitent thief returned the stolen money and begged for forgiveness.

origin.ko: 라틴어 paenitēns '후회하는'에서 왔고, paeniteō는 '뉘우치다'입니다.

senses.en: deeply or seriously thoughtful

examples.text: He sat in pensive silence, weighing his options carefully.

senses.en: showing pensive sadness

examples.text: Her pensive gaze followed the departing train long after it vanished.

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 pensif '생각에 잠긴'에서 왔고, 라틴어 pēnsō는 '무게를 달다, 곰곰이 따지다'입니다.

senses.en: A partially shaded area around the edges of a shadow, especially an eclipse.

examples.text: The other places see the penumbra of the moon's shadow fall on the earth, so the eclipse is partial, and part of the sun's disc is still visible.

senses.en: An area of uncertainty or intermediacy between two mutually exclusive states or categories.

examples.text: The new technology operates in a legal penumbra that regulators have yet to address.

origin.ko: 신라틴어 pēnumbra에서 왔으며, paene(거의) + umbra(그림자)로 '거의 그림자'라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: excessively unwilling to spend

examples.text: The penurious landlord refused to repair the heating even in midwinter.

senses.en: not having enough money to pay for necessities

examples.text: A penurious student, he lived on bread and tea for most of the winter.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 pēnūriōsus에서 왔고, 라틴어 penuria는 '결핍'입니다.

senses.en: a state of extreme poverty or destitution

examples.text: The poet died in penury, his work unrecognized until decades later.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pēnūria '결핍, 궁핍'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: A person of low rank or importance.

examples.text: He is well dressed in cheap clothing. Like an office peon whose wife works in a laundry.

senses.en: a laborer who is obliged to do menial work

examples.text: Landowners once kept entire families as peons, bound to the estate by debt.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 pedōnem '보행자'에서 왔습니다. 걸어 다니는 하인이라는 데서 말단 인물을 가리키게 되었습니다.

senses.en: Without determination by or involvement of extraneous factors; by its very nature.

examples.text: Some people say that a hangover is caused by impurities in the drink, not by the alcohol per se.

origin.ko: 라틴어 per sē '그 자체로'를 그대로 쓰는 표현입니다.

senses.en: characterized by ease and quickness in perceiving

examples.text: A percipient observer, she noticed the subtle shift in the negotiators' tone.

origin.ko: 라틴어 percipiō '완전히 파악하다'에서 왔습니다. 재빨리 붙잡아 알아채는 통찰력입니다.

senses.en: To travel from place to place, or from one country to another, especially on foot; hence, to sojourn in foreign countries.

examples.text: As a young scholar, he peregrinated across Europe, studying in a dozen universities.

origin.ko: 라틴어 peregrīnārī '외국에서 살거나 여행하다'에서 왔습니다. 땅을 가로질러 두루 다닌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: not allowing contradiction or refusal

examples.text: spoke in peremptory tones

senses.en: offensively self-assured or given to exercising usually unwarranted power

examples.text: The new supervisor's peremptory manner quickly alienated the whole team.

origin.ko: 라틴어 peremptōrius '결정적인'에서 왔고, perimō는 '없애다'입니다. 토론의 여지를 아예 없애 버리는 단호함입니다.

senses.en: Appearing or recurring again and again; recurrent.

examples.text: Change is a perennial theme in politics.

senses.en: lasting an indefinitely long time; suggesting self-renewal

examples.text: perennial happiness

senses.en: lasting three seasons or more

examples.text: the common buttercup is a popular perennial plant

origin.ko: 라틴어 perennis '해를 꿰뚫는'에서 왔습니다. 해마다 되풀이된다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: tending to betray; especially having a treacherous character as attributed to the Carthaginians by the Romans

examples.text: The king, betrayed by his perfidious advisors, lost both his throne and his army.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perfidia '배신'에서 왔고, fidēs는 '믿음'입니다. 믿음을 저버리는 성향입니다.

senses.en: an act of deliberate betrayal

examples.text: The ally's perfidy, revealed only after the treaty was signed, shocked the entire nation.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perfidia '신의를 저버림'에서 왔고, fidēs는 '믿음'입니다. fidelity와 같은 뿌리입니다.

senses.en: hasty and without attention to detail; not thorough

examples.text: The inspector gave the wiring a perfunctory glance and moved on to the next room.

senses.en: done or produced as a formality only

examples.text: The committee gave the proposal only a perfunctory review before approving it.

origin.ko: 후기 라틴어 perfunctōrius '건성인'에서 왔고, perfungor는 '해치우다'입니다. 겨우 해치우듯 형식만 채운다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: fraught with danger

examples.text: a perilous voyage across the Atlantic in a small boat

origin.ko: 옛 프랑스어 perilleus에서 왔고, peril(위험)에 -ous가 붙은 말입니다.

senses.en: Constantly travelling.

examples.text: The peripatetic conductor spent most of the year touring orchestras on three continents.

origin.ko: 그리스어 peripatētikós '이리저리 걷기 좋아하는'에서 왔습니다. 두루 걸어 다닌다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: related to the key issue but not of central importance

examples.text: energy is far from a peripheral issue in the economy

senses.en: on or near an edge or constituting an outer boundary; the outer area

examples.text: peripheral suburbs

origin.ko: 그리스어 periphéreia '둘레'에서 왔습니다. 중심이 아니라 가장자리에 있어 부수적이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: pass from physical life and lose all bodily attributes and functions necessary to sustain life

examples.text: The children perished in the fire

senses.en: To decay in such a way that it cannot be used for its original purpose

examples.text: The difficulty is that fresh foods perish due to the multiplication in them of harmful bacteria.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perīre '지나가 버리다'에서 왔고, per(통해) + īre(가다)로 이루어졌습니다. 사라져 가는 데서 죽다가 되었습니다.

senses.en: spread or diffuse through

examples.text: An atmosphere of distrust has permeated this administration

senses.en: pass through

examples.text: Water permeates sand easily

origin.ko: 라틴어 permeō '통과하다'에서 왔습니다. 속속들이 지나가며 스며든다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: working or spreading in a hidden and usually injurious way

examples.text: Critics warned of the pernicious influence of misinformation on public trust.

senses.en: exceedingly harmful

examples.text: Poverty has a pernicious effect on children's long-term health.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perniciōsus '파멸적인'에서 왔고, perniciēs는 '파괴'입니다. nex는 '죽음'이라는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: (rhetoric) the concluding section of an oration

examples.text: he summarized his main points in his peroration

origin.ko: 라틴어 perōrō '끝까지 말하다, 연설을 맺다'에서 왔습니다. 연설을 끝까지 말해 마무리하는 부분입니다.

senses.en: perform an act, usually with a negative connotation

examples.text: perpetrate a crime

origin.ko: 라틴어 perpetrāre '끝까지 해내다'에서 왔습니다. 일을 끝까지 해치운다는 뜻이 나쁜 짓을 저지른다로 쓰입니다.

senses.en: continuing forever or indefinitely

examples.text: Medieval alchemists dreamed of a perpetual source of energy and eternal youth.

senses.en: uninterrupted in time and indefinitely long continuing

examples.text: Residents complained of the perpetual noise from the highway outside their windows.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perpetuus '끊임없이 이어지는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: cause to continue or prevail

examples.text: perpetuate a myth

origin.ko: 라틴어 perpetuō '끊임없이 이어지게 하다'에서 왔고, perpetuus '영원한'이 원형입니다.

senses.en: an incidental benefit awarded for certain types of employment (especially if it is regarded as a right)

examples.text: The perquisites of this job include health insurance and a performance bonus.

senses.en: a right reserved exclusively by a particular person or group (especially a hereditary or official right)

examples.text: Private jets and motor yachts are perquisites of the rich.

origin.ko: 중세 라틴어 perquīsītum '이익을 보고 얻은 것'에서 왔습니다. 본 급여 외에 따로 얻는 부수입을 뜻합니다.

senses.en: persistent determination

examples.text: Years of perseverance finally paid off when the team published its landmark study.

origin.ko: 라틴어 persevērantia '꿋꿋함'에서 왔습니다. 끝까지 엄격하게 버티는 끈기입니다.

senses.en: be persistent, refuse to stop

examples.text: The child persisted and kept asking questions

senses.en: To continue to exist.

examples.text: Throughout the period, toothy giants persisted in the oceans. Perhaps the most spectacular was the megalodon shark.

origin.ko: 라틴어 persistere '끝까지 서 있다'에서 왔습니다. 물러나지 않고 계속 버틴다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: acutely insightful and wise

examples.text: much too perspicacious to be taken in by such a spurious argument

origin.ko: 라틴어 perspicāx '날카롭게 꿰뚫어 보는'에서 왔고, perspiciō는 '속까지 들여다보다'입니다.

senses.en: Acute discernment or understanding; insight.

examples.text: The investor's perspicacity allowed her to foresee the market crash months in advance.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perspicācitās '날카롭게 꿰뚫어 봄'에서 왔고, perspiciō는 '속까지 들여다보다'입니다.

senses.en: (of language) transparently clear; easily understandable

examples.text: The lawyer's perspicuous explanation made the complex statute easy for jurors to follow.

origin.ko: 라틴어 perspicuus '속이 환히 보이는'에서 왔습니다. 꿰뚫어 볼 수 있을 만큼 명료하다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: characterized by a lightly pert and exuberant quality

examples.text: The pert young waitress answered every complaint with a cheeky remark.

origin.ko: 중세 영어 apert '열린, 숨김없는'의 앞부분이 떨어져 나간 말입니다. 거침없이 나서는 당돌함이 되었습니다.

senses.en: stubbornly unyielding

examples.text: The pertinacious reporter pursued the story despite repeated threats from officials.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pertinax '아주 꽉 붙잡고 놓지 않는'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: having precise or logical relevance to the matter at hand

examples.text: a list of articles pertinent to the discussion

origin.ko: 라틴어 pertinēns '~에 닿는, 속하는'에서 왔습니다. 어떤 일에 닿아 있다는 데서 관련 있다는 뜻이 되었습니다.

senses.en: disturb in mind or make uneasy or cause to be worried or alarmed

examples.text: She was rather perturbed by the news that her father was seriously ill

senses.en: throw into great confusion or disorder

examples.text: Fundamentalists threaten to perturb the social order

origin.ko: 라틴어 perturbāre '완전히 어지럽히다'에서 왔고, turbō는 '휘젓다'입니다. 마음을 휘저어 불안하게 한다는 뜻입니다.

senses.en: examine or consider with attention and in detail

examples.text: Please peruse this report at your leisure

origin.ko: per-(철저히)와 use(쓰다)를 합친 말로, 원래 '다 써서 닳게 하다'였습니다. 속속들이 꼼꼼히 살핀다는 뜻만 남았습니다.

senses.en: spread or diffuse through

examples.text: Cruel wars pervade history.

origin.ko: 라틴어 pervādō '구석구석 지나가다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: spreading or spread throughout

examples.text: the pervasive odor of garlic

origin.ko: 라틴어 pervādō '구석구석 지나가다'에서 왔습니다.

senses.en: Childishly irritable.

examples.text: Lack of sleep is causing Dave's recent petulant behavior.

origin.ko: 라틴어 petulāns '건방진'에서 왔고, petō '요구하다'와 가까운 말입니다.
